annotation_description: With 4 lands already in the kept hand (Island, 2x Spirebluff Canal, Willowrush Verge), bottoming Accumulate Wisdom instead of the Island means keeping an excess land over a cheap cantrip that synergizes with the Lesson theme (Toph, Combustion Technique). The hand is already land-heavy at 4 lands with only 3 spells.

The player chose 'Spider' as the creature type for Cavern of Souls, but 'Spider' is not even among the available choices (the options are Druid, Spirit, Elf, Noble, Horror, Avatar, Vampire, Dragon, Demon, Elder). More importantly, looking at the hand, the player has Town Greeter (Human Citizen), Oblivious Bookworm (Human Wizard), Gran-Gran (Human Peasant Ally), and Superior Spider-Man (Spider Human Hero). Choosing 'Human' would allow Cavern of Souls to cast three creatures from hand with uncounterable colored mana, while 'Spider' would only help Superior Spider-Man. The reasoning mentions Spider isn't in the top 10 but says 'I will declare it anyway' — however the game requires choosing from the presented options. Since the actual choice isn't shown as resolved, but the reasoning clearly indicates a suboptimal creature type even if it were available. Among the actual choices presented, none perfectly match, but Human isn't listed either. The player should have chosen whichever type best supports their hand — likely none of these are ideal, but the reasoning about wanting Spider over Human is clearly wrong given the hand composition.

With Gran-Gran on the opponent's board (draws a card when tapped), casting Oblivious Bookworm on turn 2 would develop a 2/3 body that provides card advantage at end step, which is arguably stronger than Town Greeter's 1/1 body with mill 4. However, Town Greeter helps find lands and fill the graveyard for Superior Spider-Man, so this is debatable. The bigger question is whether Bitter Triumph should be considered to remove Gran-Gran before it generates value — Gran-Gran's cost reduction ability with Lessons in graveyard could be very dangerous, and it draws cards whenever it taps. Using Bitter Triumph now (discarding a card) would remove a key engine piece, though it costs a card from hand.

The player has 2 mana available (Cavern of Souls + Starting Town) and could cast Oblivious Bookworm (costs {G}{U}). Starting Town can pay 1 life for any color, giving green, and Cavern of Souls was likely set to a creature type. However, looking more carefully: Cavern of Souls adds {C} or colored mana only for the chosen creature type. If the chosen type matches Bookworm's types (Human/Wizard), then Cavern could add {U} for it. Starting Town can add any color for 1 life, providing {G}. So casting Oblivious Bookworm was likely possible and would develop the board with a 2/3 that draws cards each end step. Holding up Bitter Triumph sounds reasonable defensively, but Bitter Triumph costs {1}{B} — the player cannot actually cast it with just Cavern of Souls and Starting Town since Cavern only adds colored mana for creature spells of the chosen type, and Bitter Triumph is not a creature spell. So the reasoning about holding up Bitter Triumph is flawed. The player should have deployed Oblivious Bookworm to develop their board, as they cannot actually use the mana for removal anyway.

Gran-Gran's triggered ability requires discarding a card on becoming tapped. The player discarded Steam Vents, which is a dual land they could play next turn to fix mana. Meanwhile, they have Lesson cards (Boomerang Basics, Combustion Technique, Accumulate Wisdom) that they actively want in the graveyard to power up Gran-Gran's cost reduction ability (3+ Lessons in graveyard) and to power up Combustion Technique's damage and Accumulate Wisdom's card advantage. Discarding a Lesson card here would progress toward the 3-Lesson threshold while the Steam Vents could be played as a land drop.

With 3 mana available (Cavern of Souls + 2 Starting Towns), the player could cast Town Greeter (1G) to develop the board, mill cards to potentially find lands, and start building toward their gameplan. Instead they passed with unused mana. Oblivious Bookworm (GU) was also castable. Playing a creature here would advance the board state and not waste a turn's worth of mana.

message: Select a card (to put into your hand)
annotation_description: Chose a duplicate Monument to Endurance (already had one in hand) over Steam Vents when stuck on only 2 lands. Without a third land, they can't cast Monument next turn. Steam Vents would guarantee hitting their land drop and enable casting Monument on curve.

With 4 mana available, Wistfulness can only be cast for its evoke cost (sacrificed on entry), giving at best draw 2 discard 1 (if UU was spent). Meanwhile, the opponent has an empty board - this is the perfect time to develop permanent threats. Gem25P Philo could cast both Overlord of the Balemurk for its impending cost (1B) and Oblivious Bookworm (GU) in the same turn, deploying two powerful permanents that generate ongoing card advantage.

Gem25P Philo has 4 lands (Cavern of Souls, 2 Starting Towns, Breeding Pool) and multiple castable creatures in hand but chose to cast nothing and skip the entire turn. The reasoning mentions having cast Wistfulness, but the board shows no Wistfulness in play - it was likely evoked earlier and sacrificed. With 4 mana available, they could cast Oblivious Bookworm (GU - easily paid with Breeding Pool + Starting Town) to start generating card advantage, or Town Greeter (1G) to mill and find lands, or Overlord of the Balemurk for its impending cost (1B). The opponent has an empty board with only 2 tapped lands, making this the perfect time to deploy threats. Passing with no board presence while the opponent is also developing is a significant tempo loss.

On turn 7 with 4 mana available and multiple excellent castable spells, the player passed without casting anything. This wasted an entire turn of development and forced them to discard Bringer of the Last Gift to hand size, losing a powerful finisher for nothing. The opponent had no creatures and all lands tapped, so there was zero reason to hold up mana.

Cast Boomerang Basics before making the land drop with Island. Should always play the land first to maximize available mana before committing to spell sequencing. With Island played first, they'd have 7 mana available instead of 6, which could matter for casting multiple spells this turn (e.g., Combustion Technique + Firebending Lesson).

MiMo Trash declined to cast Firebending Lesson to kill Town Greeter (1/1) with mana available and nothing else to spend it on. This would have removed a creature, added a Lesson to the graveyard (potentially relevant for Lesson synergies), and used mana that would otherwise go to waste at end of turn.

Declined Artist's Talent's loot trigger when they have TWO Monument to Endurance on the battlefield. Discarding any card would have drawn a replacement card from Artist's Talent AND triggered both Monuments (giving two choices among: draw a card, create a Treasure, or opponent loses 3 life). This is substantial free value being left on the table.

MiMo Trash declined to cast Accumulate Wisdom with 5 Lesson cards in graveyard, which would have drawn all 3 cards looked at instead of just 1. With untapped lands available and Artist's Talent also triggering for an additional loot, this is significant card advantage left on the table. The mana would likely go unused otherwise.

message: You may choose an alternative cost
annotation_description: Player cast Wistfulness for full cost (5 mana) instead of evoking it, spending all available mana. The reasoning was based on a misunderstanding of the card (thinking it strips opponent's hand - that's Deceit, not Wistfulness). Wistfulness draws 2/discards 1 (if UU spent) or exiles an artifact/enchantment (if GG spent). Evoking for 2 mana would still get the ETB triggers while leaving 3 mana open for other plays, like playing Overgrown Tomb and holding up interaction. At 8 life with the opponent likely having burn/removal, leaving mana open is important.

Named 'Nightmare' for Cavern of Souls, but Harvester of Misery is a Spirit, not a Nightmare. This means the Cavern cannot produce colored mana for any creature in the player's hand or graveyard, effectively making it a colorless-only land.
